description:
Redwood Inference’s Serving Runtime org is building a mixed-workload scheduler prototype to reduce p95 (and worst-case) tail latency when short prompts (latency-sensitive, interactive chat) contend with long prompts (prefill-heavy, throughput-oriented) on the same GPU workers. The project focuses on kernel-adjacent runtime scheduling (queueing, admission control, prefill/decode interleaving, and fairness), plus the instrumentation and benchmarking required to confidently ship.

Goals:
- Reduce p95 end-to-end latency for short prompts under mixed workloads without materially degrading overall throughput.
- Introduce a policy framework that classifies requests (short vs long, or more granular buckets) and schedules them with explicit QoS goals.
- Make improvements measurable and safe to roll out via feature flags, canary, and regression detection.

Scope:
- Runtime scheduler changes: queue model, selection policy, backpressure/load-shedding hooks, starvation bounds.
- Request classification heuristics (based on prompt length, expected decode length, or early-token signals).
- Perf suite updates: mixed prompt-length distributions, replay traces, and reproducible benchmarks across GPU SKUs.
- Observability: new metrics (queue wait, prefill/decode breakdown, per-class p50/p95), dashboards, and alerting guidance.

Non-goals:
- Major kernel rewrites (only small kernel-side instrumentation/tuning if needed).
- Customer-facing API changes (policy is internal/flagged).

Stakeholders:
- Eng Serving Runtime (Scheduling): Sofia Ivanova (EM), Lena Fischer, Marcus Reed, Julian Moore.
- Runtime architecture/perf: Noah Patel, Omar El-Sayed.
- Kernels/perf stability: Hiro Tanaka, Grace Kim, Yuki Sato.
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant.
- Product alignment (latency promises, Dedicated SLOs): Nikhil Sharma, Lauren Bishop.

Timeline (hypothetical):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): benchmark definition, trace capture, instrumentation plan, design review.
- Phase 1 (2–3 weeks): implement prototype policy behind a flag; add metrics + perf-canary scenario.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): iterate based on benchmark + staging load tests; tighten starvation/fairness guarantees.
- Phase 3 (1–2 weeks): limited production canary (subset of workers/regions); validate p95 + error budget impact; decide rollout/rollback.

Key deliverables:
- Confluence design + ADR(s), benchmark plan, profiling playbook updates.
- Linear project + execution tickets.
- GitHub PR series across runtime, perf suite, and observability.
- Slack coordination threads for design decisions and rollout.
- Optional customer-driven artifacts (support ticket, technical deep dive transcript) if triggered by escalation.

files.description: Primary design doc: problem statement (mixed short/long prompt contention), proposed queue model, scheduling algorithm options (2-queue priority, WFQ, time-slicing), fairness/starvation bounds, and feature-flag rollout plan.
Heuristics doc: how to classify requests (prompt tokens, expected output tokens, early decode signals), misclassification risk, and fallbacks when clients omit max_tokens.
Defines scheduler invariants (no starvation, bounded queue wait for short class under target load), interaction with batching, and how prefill/decode phases are accounted for in scheduling decisions.
Benchmark plan: target distributions (e.g., 70/30 short/long), prompt length histograms, concurrency/arrival processes, metrics to report (p50/p95/p99, TTFT), and acceptance thresholds.
Profiling playbook addition: how to capture traces for queue wait vs compute time, where to place spans, and how to interpret prefill/decode overlap under the new policy.
ADR capturing the decision to ship an initial two-class scheduler (short/long) behind a flag, with rationale vs alternatives (pure FCFS, strict priority, WFQ) and explicit rollout guardrails.
Standardizes latency definitions used by runtime and SRE: TTFT vs end-to-end, queue wait, prefill time, decode time, and how to compute p95 under mixed workloads.
Dashboard specification: required panels (per-class p95, queue depth, starvation detector, prefill/decode utilization), recommended filters (region, model, SKU), and alert suggestions.
SRE guidance for experimentation: which SLOs to watch, error budget considerations, canary gating criteria, and rollback triggers specific to scheduler changes.
Draft release note entry for an internal/runtime release: new scheduler experiment flag, metrics added, known limitations, and how to disable quickly.
Working kickoff notes: attendees, rough plan, initial hypotheses about long-prefill blocking, and a list of open questions/risks.
Living doc of unresolved questions: fairness targets, interaction with continuous batching, impact of streaming, and how to treat tool-calling long outputs.
Trace sampling plan: which services emit spans, sampling rates, how to label request class, and privacy considerations for prompt length logging.
Spreadsheet export: baseline mixed workload results across a few models/SKUs (p50/p95, TTFT, throughput), with notes on run-to-run variance.
Spreadsheet export: results after prototype scheduling policy (flag on), including deltas vs baseline and breakdown by short/long classes.
Rough modeling doc: simple queueing simulation assumptions, how priority affects tail, and where the model diverges from real GPU execution.
Operational checklist for canary: metrics to monitor, traffic allocation, who is on point, rollback steps, and comms template for #eng-runtime/#eng-oncall.
Observability working draft: proposed metric names, labels (model, region, request_class), cardinality concerns, and mapping to dashboards.
Table of GPU SKUs/instance types to test, with notes on which regions have capacity and which are most representative of production.
Team retro notes after canary: what worked, surprises (classification edge cases, metric noise), follow-ups for hardening or rollback.
Linear project entry issue: "Mixed-workload scheduler prototype"—goals, non-goals, milestones, and links to Confluence design/ADR.
Implement request classification (short/long) in the runtime ingress path; acceptance criteria includes metrics for class distribution and safe defaults.
Add dual-queue scheduler prototype behind feature flag; includes starvation bounds and unit tests for queue selection.
Instrument queue wait time + per-phase timing (prefill/decode) and export per-class p50/p95 metrics.
Perf suite: add mixed prompt-length scenario + replay harness; definition of done includes stable p95 measurements within variance budget.
Perf-canary: add scheduler experiment job and thresholds to alert on tail latency regressions.
SRE coordination: define canary guardrails and rollback triggers; includes checklist and oncall handoff notes.
Investigate interaction with streaming responses and partial decode; ensure scheduler does not penalize streaming TTFT.
Kernel team consult: validate whether prefill-heavy long prompts cause cache pressure; propose lightweight kernel instrumentation if needed.
Dashboard rollout: publish mixed-workload scheduler dashboard (per-class latency, queue depth) and document interpretation guidance.
PM ticket: align on customer-facing latency expectations and how Dedicated SLO reporting should interpret experiment results; includes comms guidance.
Rollout decision issue: summarize benchmark + canary data, recommend ship/iterate/rollback, and capture next steps for hardening.
PR: Add request length classification plumbing (prompt_tokens, predicted_total_tokens) and attach request_class label to internal request context.
PR: Introduce feature flag `scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled` and config wiring (per-cluster override, safe default off).
PR: Implement dual-queue scheduler (short/long) with bounded starvation; includes unit tests for queue selection and fairness under load.
PR: Add queue wait time metrics and per-class latency histograms; includes cardinality review and metric naming alignment.
PR: Scheduler instrumentation spans (queue_enter, dequeue, prefill_start, decode_start) for tracing; updates sampling guidance comments.
PR: Backpressure integration: reject/slow-path long class when queue exceeds threshold; includes config knobs and tests.
PR: Fix classification edge case when client omits max_tokens; fallback to conservative long classification and log a debug counter.
PR: Tune continuous batching interaction with new scheduler; avoids head-of-line blocking when long prefill batch forms.
PR: Add starvation detector metric (max_wait_ms_by_class) and a debug endpoint dump for queue state snapshots.
PR: Add integration tests that replay mixed workload traces and assert p95 improvement bounds + no correctness regressions.
PR: Make scheduler policy pluggable (interface + registry) to allow future multi-bucket or WFQ experiments.
PR: Optimize classification fast-path (avoid extra allocations); includes microbench results and reviewer discussion about overhead.
PR: Canary logging improvements for experiment: periodic summary of queue depths + class mix per worker.
PR: Bugfix—prevent long class from starving short when worker count is low and batcher merges incorrectly; adds regression test.
PR: Document new config knobs inline (code comments + sample config) and add a short internal changelog entry.
PR: Add mixed prompt-length distribution scenario generator; includes seed control for reproducibility and output summary tables.
PR: Add trace replay mode for scheduler experiments; supports labeling requests as short/long and exporting per-class p95.
PR: Add perf-canary job "mixed_workload_scheduler" with thresholds and auto-bisect metadata when regression detected.
PR: Add Grafana dashboard JSON for mixed-workload scheduler metrics (per-class latency, queue wait, starvation detector).
PR: Add alert rules for p95 tail regression specific to short class during experiment; includes notes to avoid paging during low traffic.
PR: Staging-only default enablement for experiment in one cluster; includes rollout/rollback steps and CI gating.
PR: Add runtime debug command to dump scheduler queues and recent dequeue decisions for incident triage.
PR: Improve metric label hygiene (model_family, region, request_class); addresses reviewer concern about label explosion.
PR: Final tweaks before canary—adjust priority ratio and time-slice parameters; includes benchmark delta discussion and sign-off.
PR: Rollback toggle + safety: ensure disabling flag returns to legacy behavior without draining issues; adds smoke tests.
